current.text: Jaylen Brown is gone from Boston. Jayson Tatum and Paul George take his place.
Experts expect him to be the third usage option at best, maybe the fourth, behind Tatum, George and Derrick White. His usage path is more crowded than last season.
Experts project him as the sixth man and main backup ball handler, not a starter. He could start and play about 32 minutes if Mike Conley takes the backup point guard role.
One expert thinks a 29-minute bench role may suit him better than a 32-minute starting role, because as a starter he would be the third usage player.
If Paul George plays only about 30 games, he would step back into the bigger role he had last season.

Experts reject the breakout and new Jalen Brunson talk. He had only about 21 to 22 percent usage last season with few teammates around, he turns 29 soon and has basically peaked. One projection is 17 to 18 points a game, a likely step back.
His strong numbers without Jaylen Brown came without Tatum and George on the floor, so experts say they do not matter now.

Experts call him a bust and a fade at his ADP and rank of about 74 to 81. One expert will have him on zero teams. Another sees a worst case of 171st and would not be surprised if he finishes outside the top 110 to 120.
At pick 95 in a 9-cat mock draft, one expert called him a good pick, not an early one.
In an auction mock he went for 6 USD. The expert sees him as no more than a 4 USD player.
One expert expects his 2P% to recover to about 59 percent, and thinks Tatum and George sharing the ball more could help his shot quality.
Boston is very deep, with at least 12 rotation-level players for a 10-man rotation.
Boston's playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games in weeks 19 to 21, one game short of the maximum.

durable.text: He is a streaky bucket-getter. He can score 40 on a hot night but also has cold nights.
He is elite on two-pointers in the paint outside the restricted area.
Blocks are his weakest category, even for a guard, so a punt BLK team loses little with him.

note: Our league paid 16 USD for him last season. The market has cooled a lot: Yahoo average cost is 3.6 USD, ESPN value is 2 USD, and one expert says he is worth no more than 4 USD, so do not pay more than about 5 USD. Threes are his best category (about 2.8 per game, +1.5 z), and he adds solid FT%, assists and low turnovers, so he fits punt BLK builds as a cheap bench or Util guard. Early in the season, check whether he starts or comes off the bench, whether he gets about 30 minutes, and whether Paul George stays healthy.
